title: Test request states and failures
summary: Implement a request reducer with explicit transitions, then design a test suite that covers loading, empty success, rejection, and retry.

scenario.briefing: The product page keeps old products visible after a failed refresh. The team wants the request logic tested before another UI change ships.

objectives.description: Select the cases a request test suite must cover.

hints: Map each action type to exactly one next state.
Starting a request always replaces the previous state with loading.
An error state carries only the message, not the old data.
A retry must be able to move from error back to loading.

misconceptions.description: Keeping stale success data after an error.
misconceptions.testDescription: An error replaces previous success data.
misconceptions.feedback: An error state should describe the failure, not a mix of failure and old data. Keeping both makes the screen lie about what is current.

misconceptions.description: Ignoring the start action during a retry.
misconceptions.testDescription: Starting a request enters the loading state.
misconceptions.feedback: A retry starts a new request. If the reducer ignores start, the screen keeps showing the old error while the request is in flight.
A happy-path-only suite cannot detect stale data or a missing retry. Failure and empty-success cases are part of the behavior, not extras.

sections.title: A request is a state machine
sections.body: Idle, loading, success, and error are distinct states. A reducer makes the transitions explicit, so a failed refresh cannot leave stale success data on screen.

sections.title: Test the transition, not the markup
sections.body: Start from the state before the action and assert the state after it. A test for the error transition fails when the reducer silently keeps the previous data.

sections.title: Design the failure cases first
sections.body: A useful request test covers loading, success, empty success, rejection, and a retry after failure. A suite that only checks the happy path cannot catch the bugs users report.

steps.title: Reduce request actions
steps.prompt: Edit requestState.ts. Implement reduceRequest so start, success, and error each produce the correct state and an error never keeps stale data.
hints: Use a switch on action.type and return a full state object per branch.
The start branch returns only { status: "loading" }.
The success branch keeps action.data and the success status.
The error branch returns only the message and the error status.

steps.title: Design the request test suite
steps.prompt: Select every case the request test suite must cover. Leave out cases that test the wrong behavior.
hints: Start with the four states the interface can render.
Add the retry transition because it starts a second request.
Reject cases that preserve stale data or encourage brittle markup snapshots.
Keep only behaviors a user can observe.

cases.label: Shows progress while the request is pending.
Renders the returned products after a successful response.
Shows an empty-state message when the response contains no products.
Shows the error message and a retry action after a rejected request.
Moves from error back to loading when the user retries.
Keeps the previous success data visible after a failed refresh.
Asserts the exact HTML string of the entire page.
Calls setState after unmount without a guard.

steps.explanation: The suite needs loading, success, empty success, error, and retry. Keeping stale data contradicts the error state, exact page snapshots are brittle, and an unguarded post-unmount update is the bug rather than the expected behavior.

accessibility.summary: The workspace is keyboard accessible. Use the editor with Tab and run checks with Ctrl+Enter; every result is announced in text.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Tab moves between the editor, hints, and results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks. Hint buttons reveal one level at a time.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, pass or fail state, and the missing or forbidden source fragment.
